case_studies.title: Experimental Performance of a 5G N78 Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface: From Controlled Measurements to Commercial Network Deployment
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a real-world experimental analysis of a modular reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) prototype designed to operate in the 5G N78 band. Unlike most RIS studies in the literature that focus on simulations or controlled setups, the proposed system is validated through three phases consisting of indoor measurements, outdoor long-range tests, and deployment in a live commercial 5G standalone network. The RIS is exploited to enhance coverage in a non-line-of-sight (NLoS) zone, identified through baseline drive tests. Results show promising gains in RSRP and SINR, while also r
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the enhancement of coverage in non-line-of-sight zones in 5G networks. The AI approach employed is the use of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) prototype designed to operate in the 5G N78 band. The outcome of the study shows promising gains in RSRP and SINR, indicating the potential of RIS technology to improve network coverage.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this technology, AI practitioners can explore the use of RIS prototypes in their own network deployment scenarios, taking into account the specific frequency bands and environmental conditions of their use case. By conducting thorough measurements and tests, practitioners can validate the performance of RIS technology and identify opportunities for improvement.
case_studies.monetisation: The RIS technology developed in this study has clear monetisation potential as a product opportunity for network operators and equipment manufacturers. Companies can leverage this technology to enhance their network coverage and provide better services to their customers, resulting in increased revenue and competitiveness.

case_studies.title: Design Structure Matrix Modularization with Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Design Structure Matrix (DSM) modularization, the task of partitioning system elements into cohesive modules, is a fundamental combinatorial challenge in engineering design. Traditional methods treat modularization as a pure graph optimization, without access to the engineering context embedded in the system. Building on prior work on LLM-based combinatorial optimization for DSM sequencing, this paper extends the method to modularization across five cases and three backbone LLMs. Our method achieves near-reference quality within 30 iterations without requiring specialized optimization code. Co
case_studies.summary: The problem of Design Structure Matrix (DSM) modularization is a fundamental challenge in engineering design, where traditional methods treat modularization as a pure graph optimization without considering the engineering context. This paper proposes an AI approach using Large Language Models (LLMs) to extend the method to modularization, achieving near-reference quality within 30 iterations. The outcome of this approach is a significant improvement in DSM modularization, with potential applications in various engineering design fields.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this method by utilizing LLMs to optimize combinatorial problems, such as DSM modularization, and achieve near-reference quality results without requiring specialized optimization code. To implement this approach, practitioners should consider selecting suitable backbone LLMs and fine-tuning them for their specific use case.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed method has a clear product opportunity in the engineering design industry, where companies can develop and market software solutions that utilize LLMs for DSM modularization. This can help companies improve their design efficiency and productivity, leading to cost savings and competitive advantages in the market.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is hindered by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. The authors propose a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization, evaluating model-hardware pairs under cost, energy, and time metrics. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can use the cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate and select the most suitable model-hardware pairs for their specific use case. By considering the trade-offs between cost, energy, and time, practitioners can optimize their VLA models for efficient on-robot deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The research provides a concrete business opportunity for companies developing edge devices and AI models for robotics, as it highlights the potential for efficient and cost-effective on-robot deployment. By leveraging the insights from this study, companies can design and market optimized AI-powered robots for various applications, such as manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare.

case_studies.title: PhyCo: Learning Controllable Physical Priors for Generative Motion
case_studies.abstract: Modern video diffusion models excel at appearance synthesis but still struggle with physical consistency: objects drift, collisions lack realistic rebound, and material responses seldom match their underlying properties. We present PhyCo, a framework that introduces continuous, interpretable, and physically grounded control into video generation. Our approach integrates three key components: (i) a large-scale dataset of over 100K photorealistic simulation videos where friction, restitution, deformation, and force are systematically varied across diverse scenarios; (ii) physics-supervised fine-
case_studies.summary: Modern video diffusion models struggle with physical consistency, resulting in unrealistic object interactions and movements. The authors introduce PhyCo, a framework that incorporates physics-supervised fine-tuning and a large-scale dataset of photorealistic simulation videos to generate more realistic motion. By integrating physical priors into video generation, PhyCo achieves more realistic and controllable motion synthesis.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can integrate physical constraints and simulation data into their generative models to improve realism and control. By leveraging large-scale datasets and physics-supervised fine-tuning, developers can create more realistic and engaging video content.
case_studies.monetisation: The PhyCo framework has the potential to be monetized in the video game and film industries, where realistic motion synthesis is crucial for immersive experiences. Companies can license the technology or develop products that utilize PhyCo's physics-based video generation capabilities, such as AI-powered video editing tools or virtual reality platforms.

case_studies.title: DEFault++: Automated Fault Detection, Categorization, and Diagnosis for Transformer Architectures
case_studies.abstract: Transformer models are widely deployed in critical AI applications, yet faults in their attention mechanisms, projections, and other internal components often degrade behavior silently without raising runtime errors. Existing fault diagnosis techniques often target generic deep neural networks and cannot identify which transformer component is responsible for an observed symptom. In this article, we present DEFault++, a hierarchical learning-based diagnostic technique that operates at three level of abstraction: it detects whether a fault is present, classifies it into one of 12 transformer-sp
case_studies.summary: The problem of silent faults in transformer models can lead to degraded behavior without raising runtime errors, making it challenging to identify and diagnose issues. The authors propose DEFault++, a hierarchical learning-based diagnostic technique that operates at three levels of abstraction to detect, classify, and diagnose faults in transformer architectures. The outcome of this approach is a more robust and reliable transformer model that can identify and address faults effectively.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from DEFault++ by incorporating hierarchical learning-based diagnostic techniques into their own transformer models to improve fault detection and diagnosis. By doing so, they can develop more robust and reliable AI systems that can operate effectively in critical applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The DEFault++ technique has clear product opportunities in the AI industry, particularly in applications where transformer models are widely used, such as natural language processing and computer vision. Companies can develop and market DEFault++ as a diagnostic tool or integrate it into their existing AI products to improve reliability and performance.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed through a novel approach that optimizes model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This is achieved by using a feasible-first exploration strategy in a hierarchical mixed-variable search space, which reduces the number of invalid configurations evaluated. The outcome is a more efficient optimization process that can handle crash-prone search spaces, leading to improved deployment of machine learning models.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by using feasible-first exploration strategies in their optimization processes, especially when dealing with constrained and hierarchical search spaces. By doing so, they can reduce the number of invalid configurations evaluated and improve the efficiency of their optimization processes.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach has clear monetisation potential as it can be integrated into existing MLOps pipelines, allowing companies to optimize their machine learning model deployment and reduce costs associated with invalid configurations. This can be achieved by developing a product or service that offers feasible-first exploration for constrained ML deployment optimization, which can be sold to companies looking to improve their machine learning model deployment efficiency.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was used to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulatin
case_studies.summary: The study evaluates the robustness of a foundation segmentation model under simulated domain shifts in abdominal CT scans, which is crucial for reliable spleen segmentation. The model, Segment Anything Model (SAM), is tested using a systematic slice-level robustness audit on 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes. The outcome of this study provides insights into the model's performance under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts, highlighting areas for improvement.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners can use the standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty in their own models. By doing so, they can systematically evaluate the robustness of their models under various domain shifts, leading to more reliable and generalizable results.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing more robust and reliable medical imaging models, which can be licensed to healthcare providers or integrated into existing medical imaging software. This can lead to improved patient outcomes and reduced costs associated with inaccurate diagnoses or repeated scans.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The increasing threat of quantum computers to traditional cryptography poses a significant challenge to internet infrastructure, particularly in the deployment of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) which introduces larger certificate chain sizes. This study evaluates the impact of PQC on Time to First Byte (TTFB) in TLS deployments, focusing on CDN-centric conditions. The outcome provides valuable insights into the latency costs associated with transitioning to quantum-safe certificates.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the implications of PQC deployment on network latency and develop strategies to mitigate these effects, such as optimizing certificate chain sizes or improving network infrastructure. By doing so, they can ensure a smoother transition to quantum-safe cryptography and minimize the impact on user experience.
case_studies.monetisation: The research on PQC deployment challenges presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in cybersecurity and network optimization, as they can develop and market solutions to mitigate the latency costs associated with quantum-safe certificates. Moreover, the study's findings can be used to inform the development of new products and services that address the needs of organizations transitioning to PQC.

case_studies.title: 3D Reconstruction Techniques in the Manufacturing Domain: Applications, Research Opportunities and Use Cases
case_studies.abstract: This comprehensive review examines the evolution and the current state of the art in three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction techniques in manufacturing applications. The analysis covers both traditional approaches and emerging deep learning methods, showing a critical research gap in unified 3d reconstruction frameworks. Through systematic review of 106 recent publications, we classify reconstruction techniques into three primary categories: data acquisition, point cloud generation, post-processing and applications. Non-contact methods, particularly structured light scanning and stereo vision,
case_studies.summary: The manufacturing domain faces challenges in accurately reconstructing 3D models, hindering efficient production and quality control. This study reviews traditional and emerging deep learning methods for 3D reconstruction, highlighting a gap in unified frameworks. The analysis classifies techniques into data acquisition, point cloud generation, post-processing, and applications, paving the way for further research and development.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings by exploring non-contact methods like structured light scanning and stereo vision for 3D reconstruction in manufacturing. By understanding the current state of the art and research gaps, practitioners can develop more effective and unified 3D reconstruction frameworks.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetised by developing and marketing unified 3D reconstruction frameworks and software solutions tailored to the manufacturing industry. Companies can leverage these solutions to improve production efficiency, quality control, and supply chain management, offering a significant business opportunity.

case_studies.title: A Pattern Language for Resilient Visual Agents
case_studies.abstract: Integrating multimodal foundation models into enterprise ecosystems presents a fundamental software architecture challenge. Architects must balance competing quality attributes: the high latency and non-determinism of vision language action (VLA) models versus the strict determinism and real-time performance required by enterprise control loops. In this study, we propose an architectural pattern language for visual agents that separates fast, deterministic reflexes from slow, probabilistic supervision. It consists of four architectural design patterns: (1) Hybrid Affordance Integration, (2) Ad
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the challenge of integrating multimodal foundation models into enterprise ecosystems, which requires balancing competing quality attributes such as latency and determinism. The proposed solution is an architectural pattern language for visual agents that separates fast, deterministic reflexes from slow, probabilistic supervision. This approach consists of four architectural design patterns that can help architects design more resilient visual agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by separating their model's decision-making process into fast, deterministic reflexes and slow, probabilistic supervision, allowing for more robust and efficient visual agents. By using the proposed design patterns, architects can create more scalable and maintainable visual agent systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed architectural pattern language can be monetised by creating a commercial framework or toolkit that implements these design patterns, allowing enterprises to easily integrate multimodal foundation models into their ecosystems. This framework could be sold as a software product or offered as a service, providing a clear product opportunity for companies operating in the AI and automation space.

case_studies.title: ITS-Mina: A Harris Hawks Optimization-Based All-MLP Framework with Iterative Refinement and External Attention for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
case_studies.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting plays a pivotal role in numerous real-world applications, including financial analysis, energy management, and traffic planning. While Transformer-based architectures have gained popularity for this task, recent studies reveal that simpler MLP-based models can achieve competitive or superior performance with significantly reduced computational cost. In this paper, we propose ITS-Mina, a novel all-MLP framework for multivariate time series forecasting that integrates three key innovations: (1) an iterative refinement mechanism that progressively enhances tem
case_studies.summary: Multivariate time series forecasting is a crucial task in various real-world applications, and the proposed ITS-Mina framework aims to improve its accuracy and efficiency. The ITS-Mina framework utilizes an all-MLP architecture with iterative refinement and external attention mechanisms to achieve competitive performance. The outcome of this approach is a simpler and more efficient model that can potentially outperform more complex Transformer-based architectures.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by exploring the use of simpler MLP-based models for multivariate time series forecasting tasks, and incorporating iterative refinement and external attention mechanisms to improve performance. By doing so, they can potentially reduce computational costs and achieve competitive or superior results.
case_studies.monetisation: The ITS-Mina framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies operating in industries that rely heavily on multivariate time series forecasting, such as finance or energy management, where accurate predictions can have a significant impact on decision-making and revenue. By developing and marketing a product based on the ITS-Mina framework, companies can offer a more efficient and effective solution for multivariate time series forecasting tasks.

case_studies.title: Computing Equilibrium beyond Unilateral Deviation
case_studies.abstract: Most familiar equilibrium concepts, such as Nash and correlated equilibrium, guarantee only that no single player can improve their utility by deviating unilaterally. They offer no guarantees against profitable coordinated deviations by coalitions. Although the literature proposes solution concepts that provide stability against multilateral deviations (\emph{e.g.}, strong Nash and coalition-proof equilibrium), these generally fail to exist. In this paper, we study an alternative solution concept that minimizes coalitional deviation incentives, rather than requiring them to vanish, and is ther
case_studies.summary: The problem of traditional equilibrium concepts is that they only guarantee stability against unilateral deviations, leaving them vulnerable to coordinated deviations by coalitions. The authors propose a new solution concept that minimizes coalitional deviation incentives, providing a more robust alternative to existing approaches. This new concept has the potential to improve the stability and reliability of multi-agent systems, but its practical applications and outcomes are still theoretical and require further development.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can focus on developing algorithms that can identify and mitigate coalitional deviations in multi-agent systems, using techniques such as game theory and machine learning. By incorporating this concept into their designs, practitioners can create more robust and stable systems that can withstand coordinated deviations and improve overall performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The concept of minimizing coalitional deviation incentives has potential business applications in areas such as auction design, supply chain management, and cybersecurity, where coalition formation and deviation can have significant financial impacts. Companies can develop products and services that utilize this concept to optimize their operations and improve their bottom line, such as designing more stable and efficient auctions or developing strategies to prevent coalition-based attacks.

case_studies.title: Splitting Argumentation Frameworks with Collective Attacks and Supports
case_studies.abstract: This work proposes novel splitting techniques for argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. We base our studies on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs) which generalize argumentation frameworks with collective attacks (SETAFs), as well as bipolar argumentation frameworks (BAFs), by incorporating both collective attacks and supports. Notably, BSAFs establish a crucial link to structured argumentation as they naturally capture general (potentially non-flat) assumption-based argumentation. The increase in expressiveness calls for diverse forms o
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the need for novel splitting techniques in argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. The AI approach proposed is based on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs), which generalize argumentation frameworks with collective attacks and supports. The outcome of this study is a more expressive and general framework for argumentation that can capture complex assumption-based argumentation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the insights from this study by exploring the use of BSAFs in their own argumentation-based systems, particularly in applications where collective attacks and supports are relevant. By adopting BSAFs, practitioners can potentially increase the expressiveness and flexibility of their argumentation frameworks, leading to more effective and nuanced decision-making.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity based on this research is the development of argumentation-based decision support systems that can be applied in various industries, such as law, medicine, or finance. Such systems could be sold as software products or services, offering customers the ability to analyze complex arguments and make more informed decisions.

case_studies.title: Mapping the Methodological Space of Classroom Interaction Research: Scale, Duration, and Modality in an Age of AI
case_studies.abstract: Research on classroom interaction has long been divided between large-scale observation and in-depth ethnographic work. We propose a framework mapping this methodological space along three dimensions--scale, duration, and modality--where a study's position shapes what it reveals and obscures. We illustrate it through contrasting studies of dialogic teaching--Howe et al. (2019) and Snell and Lefstein (2018)--and an interview with the lead researchers, organized around three questions: what can be operationalized, what mechanisms become visible, and what translates to practice. We then examine h
case_studies.summary: The study explores the methodological space of classroom interaction research, proposing a framework to map the space along three dimensions: scale, duration, and modality. The AI approach involves analyzing and contrasting existing studies of dialogic teaching to illustrate the framework. The outcome is a deeper understanding of the trade-offs and opportunities in designing classroom interaction research studies.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this framework, AI practitioners can use it to inform the design of their own studies, considering the trade-offs between scale, duration, and modality. By doing so, they can optimize their study design to reveal the most relevant insights and mechanisms, and translate them into practice.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of AI-powered tools for analyzing and optimizing classroom interaction, which could be marketed to educational institutions. Such tools could provide educators with actionable insights to improve teaching practices and student outcomes, generating revenue through licensing or subscription-based models.

case_studies.title: RHyVE: Competence-Aware Verification and Phase-Aware Deployment for LLM-Generated Reward Hypotheses
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make reward design in reinforcement learning substantially more scalable, but generated rewards are not automatically reliable training objectives. Existing work has focused primarily on generating, evolving, or selecting reward candidates, while paying less attention to when such candidates can be verified and deployed during policy optimization. We study this deployment-time problem by treating generated rewards as reward hypotheses whose utility depends on the competence of the current policy and the phase of training. We propose \textsc{RHyVE}, a competence-awa
case_studies.summary: The problem of unreliable training objectives in reinforcement learning is addressed by proposing a competence-aware verification and phase-aware deployment approach for large language model-generated reward hypotheses. The AI approach, RHyVE, treats generated rewards as reward hypotheses whose utility depends on the competence of the current policy and the phase of training. The outcome is a more scalable and reliable reward design process, but the study is still in its theoretical phase and lacks concrete metrics or results.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the RHyVE approach by considering the competence of their current policy and the phase of training when deploying generated reward hypotheses, allowing for more informed decision-making. By treating generated rewards as hypotheses, practitioners can better evaluate their utility and reliability during the training process.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity for RHyVE is in the development of more efficient and scalable reinforcement learning systems, which could be marketed to companies looking to improve their autonomous systems or decision-making processes. However, the concept is still purely academic and would require significant development and testing to become a viable product.

case_studies.title: To Build or Not to Build? Factors that Lead to Non-Development or Abandonment of AI Systems
case_studies.abstract: Responsible AI research typically focuses on examining the use and impacts of deployed AI systems. Yet, there is currently limited visibility into the pre-deployment decisions to pursue building such systems in the first place. Decisions taken in the earlier stages of development shape which systems are ultimately released, and therefore represent potential, but underexplored, points for intervention. As such, this paper investigates factors influencing AI non-development and abandonment throughout the development lifecycle. Specifically, we first perform a scoping review of academic literatur
case_studies.summary: The problem of AI system non-development and abandonment is a significant concern, as it can lead to wasted resources and missed opportunities. This paper investigates the factors influencing AI non-development and abandonment throughout the development lifecycle using a scoping review of academic literature. The outcome of this study can provide insights into the decision-making process behind AI system development and deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by carefully evaluating the feasibility and potential impact of their AI projects before investing significant resources. By considering the factors that lead to non-development and abandonment, practitioners can make more informed decisions and increase the likelihood of successful AI system deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The insights gained from this study can be monetised by developing consulting services or tools that help organisations assess the viability of their AI projects and make data-driven decisions. Additionally, the study's findings can be used to create training programs or workshops that teach AI practitioners how to evaluate and mitigate the risks associated with AI system development and deployment.

case_studies.title: SpecVQA: A Benchmark for Spectral Understanding and Visual Question Answering in Scientific Images
case_studies.abstract: Spectra are a prevalent yet highly information-dense form of scientific imagery, presenting substantial challenges to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) due to their unstructured and domain-specific characteristics. Here we introduce SpecVQA, a professional scientific-image benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding, covering 7 representative spectrum types with expert-annotated question-answer pairs. The aim comprises two aspects: spectra scientific QA evaluation and corresponding underlying task evaluation. SpecVQA contains 620 figures and 3100 QA p
case_studies.summary: The SpecVQA benchmark addresses the challenge of understanding scientific spectral images, which are dense with information and difficult for multimodal large language models to interpret. This benchmark uses a dataset of 620 figures and 3100 question-answer pairs to evaluate the ability of models to answer questions about spectral images. By establishing a professional scientific-image benchmark, SpecVQA aims to improve the performance of multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this benchmark, AI practitioners can use SpecVQA to fine-tune their multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding, allowing them to improve their model's performance on domain-specific tasks. By utilizing SpecVQA, researchers can develop more accurate models for spectral image analysis, which can be applied to various scientific fields such as chemistry, physics, and materials science.
case_studies.monetisation: The SpecVQA benchmark presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in scientific image analysis, as it can be used to develop more accurate models for spectral image interpretation. This can lead to the creation of products and services that provide valuable insights for researchers and scientists, such as automated spectral image analysis tools or spectral image-based consulting services.

case_studies.title: Exploring Interaction Paradigms for LLM Agents in Scientific Visualization
case_studies.abstract: This paper examines how different types of large language model (LLM) agents perform on scientific visualization (SciVis) tasks, where users generate visualization workflows from natural-language instructions. We compare three primary interaction paradigms, including domain-specific agents with structured tool use, computer-use agents, and general-purpose coding agents, by evaluating eight representative agents across 15 benchmark tasks and measuring visualization quality, efficiency, robustness, and computational cost. We further analyze interaction modalities, including code scripts and mode
case_studies.summary: The problem of efficiently generating visualization workflows from natural-language instructions in scientific visualization tasks is addressed through the use of large language model (LLM) agents. The AI approach involves comparing the performance of three primary interaction paradigms, including domain-specific agents, computer-use agents, and general-purpose coding agents, across 15 benchmark tasks. The outcome of this study provides insights into the effectiveness of different LLM agents in scientific visualization tasks, highlighting their potential for improving workflow efficiency and visualization quality.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by considering the choice of interaction paradigm and agent type when designing LLM-based systems for scientific visualization tasks, and evaluating their performance using metrics such as visualization quality, efficiency, and computational cost. By analyzing the results of this study, practitioners can identify the most effective approaches for their specific use cases and improve the overall performance of their systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The research in this study can be monetized by developing and marketing LLM-based tools and platforms for scientific visualization, targeting industries such as healthcare, finance, and education, where data visualization is a critical component of decision-making. Companies can also offer customized LLM-based solutions for specific scientific visualization tasks, providing a competitive edge in the market and generating revenue through subscription-based models or consulting services.

case_studies.title: Graph World Models: Concepts, Taxonomy, and Future Directions
case_studies.abstract: As one of the mainstream models of artificial intelligence, world models allow agents to learn the representation of the environment for efficient prediction and planning. However, classical world models based on flat tensors face several key problems, including noise sensitivity, error accumulation and weak reasoning. To address these limitations, many recent studies use graph structure to decompose the environment into entity nodes and interactive edges, and model virtual environments in a structured space. This paper systematically formalizes and unifies these emerging graph-based works und
case_studies.summary: The paper addresses the limitations of classical world models, which face issues such as noise sensitivity and error accumulation. The authors propose using graph structure to decompose the environment into entity nodes and interactive edges, allowing for more efficient prediction and planning. This approach enables agents to learn the representation of the environment in a structured space, potentially leading to improved performance in various tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can utilize graph-based techniques to model complex environments, allowing for more accurate and efficient prediction and planning. By representing the environment as a graph, agents can better capture relationships between entities and make more informed decisions.
case_studies.monetisation: The concept of graph world models has potential applications in fields such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and video games, where accurate environment modeling is crucial. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more advanced and realistic simulations, leading to improved training and testing of AI agents.
